questions.question: How many rows are in a truth table for 2 variables?
questions.explanation: 2 variables = 2² = 4 rows.

questions.question: What does a truth table display?
questions.explanation: Truth tables show all possible input-output combinations.

questions.question: How many rows for 3 propositional variables?
questions.explanation: 3 variables = 2³ = 8 rows.

questions.question: What is the main connective in a truth table?
questions.explanation: Main connective is evaluated last.

questions.question: When is p∧q true?
options: When p is true or q is true
When both p and q are true
questions.explanation: Conjunction requires both true.

questions.question: When is p∨q false?
questions.explanation: Disjunction is false only when both false.

questions.question: What does the final column show?
questions.explanation: Final column shows the complete expression.

questions.question: How do you verify a tautology?
questions.explanation: Tautologies are true in all cases.

questions.question: When is p→q false?
options: When p is true and q is false
questions.explanation: Implication is false only in this case.

questions.question: How are truth tables used?
questions.explanation: Truth tables verify logical relationships.

questions.question: How many rows does a truth table with 4 propositional variables have?
questions.explanation: 4 variables give 2^4 = 16 possible truth assignments.

questions.question: What does each row of a truth table represent?
options: One possible truth assignment to the variables
questions.explanation: Each row fixes one combination of truth values for the atomic variables.

questions.question: After filling in the variable columns, what is computed next in a truth table?
questions.explanation: Subformulas are evaluated inside-out before the main connective.

questions.question: A formula whose final truth table column contains only True is a what?
questions.explanation: An all-True final column means the formula holds under every assignment.

questions.question: A formula whose final truth table column contains only False is a what?
questions.explanation: An all-False final column means the formula fails under every assignment.

questions.question: A formula whose final column mixes True and False values is a what?
questions.explanation: A contingency is true under some assignments and false under others.

questions.question: To show premises entail a conclusion with a truth table, you check that the conclusion is true in which rows?
options: Rows where at least one premise is true
Rows where all premises are true
Rows where the conclusion is false
questions.explanation: Entailment holds when no row makes all premises true and the conclusion false.

questions.question: Two formulas are logically equivalent when what holds in a shared truth table?
options: They have the same number of operators
They share at least one true row
questions.explanation: Identical final columns mean the formulas agree under every assignment.

questions.question: In the truth table for p⊕q, which rows are True?
options: Rows where p and q match
Rows where p and q differ
questions.explanation: XOR is true in the True-False and False-True rows.

questions.question: A truth table with n input variables has how many rows?
questions.explanation: Each variable doubles the possible assignments: 2^n rows.

questions.question: In the row where p=True and q=False, what is the value of ¬p∨q?
questions.explanation: ¬p = False and q = False, so ¬p∨q = False∨False = False.

questions.question: In the row where p=True and q=False, what is the value of (p∧q)→p?
questions.explanation: p∧q = False, and an implication with false antecedent is true.

questions.question: In testing an argument, what is a row called where all premises are true but the conclusion is false?
questions.explanation: A single counterexample row proves the argument invalid.

questions.question: How does the column for ¬p relate to the column for p?
options: Opposite truth value in every row
True only in the last row
questions.explanation: Negation flips every entry of the operand's column.

questions.question: If every row with all-true premises also has a true conclusion, the argument is what?
questions.explanation: Absence of counterexample rows makes the argument valid; soundness additionally requires actually true premises.

questions.question: How many truth assignments to p, q, r make p→q false?
questions.explanation: p→q fails only when p=True and q=False; r is free, giving 2 assignments.
